title: OIPS motor module (private car)
description: Benefit vocabulary and line-specific fields for private car insurance. Codes are the unit of comparison: two products are compared code by code.

anyOf.description: Liability for death or injury to other people. Compulsory under road traffic law.
Liability for damage to other people's property.
Damage to the insured car by fire, lightning or explosion.
Loss of or damage to the insured car by theft or attempted theft.
Damage to the insured car from an accident or malicious damage, regardless of fault.
Repair or replacement of windscreen and windows, usually without affecting the no claims discount.
A replacement car while the insured car is repaired.
A like-for-like or larger hire car, including after theft or a write-off.
Replacement with a new car of the same make and model if the insured car is written off or stolen within a qualifying period of first registration.
Fixed benefit for death or specified serious injury of the driver (and sometimes spouse or passengers) in an accident in the car.
Medical costs for the driver and passengers after an accident.
Loss of or damage to belongings in the car.
Permanently fitted audio, navigation and entertainment equipment.
Replacement of child car seats after an accident, whether or not visibly damaged.
Replacement keys, fobs and lock changes if keys are lost or stolen.
Draining and flushing the engine after filling with the wrong fuel.
Damage to an owned electric vehicle battery.
Charging cables, portable chargers and home wallboxes, and liability arising from their use.
Policyholder driving a car they do not own. coverBasis states the level of cover; usually third party only.
Cover while driving abroad. coverBasis and limits (units: days) state level and duration; territories lists where.
No excess and no loss of no claims discount when hit by an identified uninsured driver who is at fault.
No loss of no claims discount for a vandalism claim.
Guarantee on repairs carried out by the insurer's approved repairer.
Protects the no claims discount from being reduced after a set number of claims.
Roadside assistance and recovery.
Legal costs to recover uninsured losses (excess, injury compensation, loss of earnings) after a non-fault accident.
Third party liability while towing a trailer or caravan.
Onward travel or overnight accommodation after an accident.
Refunds the policyholder's excess after a claim.
Pays the difference between the write-off settlement and the finance outstanding or original price.
Repair or replacement of damaged tyres and alloy wheels.
Cosmetic repair of minor scratches, scuffs and dents.
Only when the car is repaired by the insurer's approved repairer.
Not if the car is written off or stolen and not recovered.
Only after a total loss or unrecovered theft.
Only when a third party is at fault.
Only when the other driver's details are known.
Only within the benefit's qualifyingPeriod after first registration or purchase.
Only when the policyholder is the first registered keeper.
Only when the other car has its own valid insurance.
Only for the policyholder, not named drivers.
A circumstance not in this list; describe it in summary.
Theft when keys were left in or on the car.
Theft when the car was left unlocked or with windows open.
Claims where undeclared modifications contributed.
Mechanical, electrical or electronic breakdown and wear and tear.
Driver over the drink or drug driving limit.
Driver without a valid licence for the car.
Racing, rallies, track days or speed testing.
Damage caused deliberately by a family member or a person living with the policyholder.
Loss through fraudulent sale or deception.
Use for hire and reward, ride-hailing or food delivery.
Use on airport airside areas.
War, terrorism and related risks beyond legal minimums.
Loss of value after a repair.
An exclusion not in this list; describe it in summary.
Report any incident within a set time, even with no intention to claim.
Keep the car roadworthy with a valid MOT.
Store keyless entry fobs in a signal-blocking pouch or box.
Keep the car in a locked garage overnight.
Keep a telematics device or app active.
Fit and use a specified alarm, immobiliser or tracker.
Stay within the declared annual mileage.
Only drivers named on the schedule may drive.
A condition not in this list; describe it in summary.
Repair at the roadside, or a tow to a local garage, away from home.
Recovery of the car and passengers to any one UK destination.
Assistance at or near the policyholder's home.
Hire car, onward travel or overnight accommodation if the car cannot be fixed the same day.
Roadside assistance and recovery while driving in Europe.
Covers the policyholder in any car, as driver or passenger, not only the insured car.
Recovery of a caravan or trailer being towed.
Pays for garage parts and labour after a breakdown, not just the call-out.

else.description: Only breakdown has a feature vocabulary in this version.

productCodes.description: Applies the motor vocabularies to every code-bearing field of a product document.

quoteCodes.description: Applies the motor vocabularies to every code-bearing field of a quote document.

vehicleUseOffered.description: Classes of use a customer may select.

writeOffSettlement.description: How the car is valued if written off or stolen.

motorRisk.description: The rating facts a quote was priced on, banded where possible. Contains no names, addresses or registration numbers, but in combination may still identify the customer.

ref.description: Document-local label, e.g. d1, that excesses use to point at this driver.
